solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S018-01.notes: Page-long looping sentences that eventually reach the point = circuitous. Terse is the opposite; didactic and cryptic aren't supported. Main barrier is knowing the word 'circuitous'.

S018-02.notes: Praise plus warning = mixed feelings = ambivalent. Effusive and scathing are each one-sided; perfunctory doesn't fit the detailed comments.

S018-03.notes: The note is about screen time vs sleep; D compares sleep across the extreme groups. A uses test scores (trap). B gives only one group. C brings in an unsupported 'passing' idea.

flags: minor: the passage line says 'The following text is adapted from a poem', but no poem text follows, only the claim. Official wording is usually like 'In the poem, the speaker expresses...'. Rephrase so the claim reads clearly as the claim.
S018-04.notes: A maple planted in April that is already scarlet and bare shows surprise at time passing quickly. D says the opposite (long, slow); C shows sameness; A is routine.

S018-05.notes: The clay is found only inland and there is no evidence of travel, so trade is most likely. B contradicts 'only inland'; C contradicts 'no evidence of travel'; D is irrelevant.

S018-06.notes: Storing water causes survival without rain, so it is cause and effect.

flags: minor: D is the only choice that hits both goals (late start + amount accomplished), so a quick keyword match solves it; typical for this type.
S018-07.notes: D names the mid-fifties start and the 145,000 specimens. A, B and C each miss one goal or both.

S018-08.notes: 'A number of X' takes a plural verb, so 'have found'. 'Has found' is a common trap for students who treat 'number' as the singular subject. C and D leave the sentence without a main verb.

S018-09.notes: The subject 'team' is singular, and 'engineers' and 'bridge' come between the subject and the verb. Habitual present ('every spring') gives 'submits'. B, C and D are all plural forms.

S018-10.notes: The 'however' sentence notes uneven rates and some stable glaciers, which qualifies the claim. A describes sentence 2; B overstates ('growing everywhere'); D is not in the text.
